questions.question: "His friend as well as I ___ going to take part in it." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: When subjects are connected by 'as well as', the verb agrees with the main subject ('His friend'), which is singular, so 'is' is correct.

questions.question: When subjects are joined by 'Either...or' or 'Neither...nor', the verb agrees with:
options: The nearest subject to the verb
questions.rationale: With correlative conjunctions like 'Either...or' and 'Neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject — the one closest to the verb.

questions.question: "The car along with five persons ___ come to this city." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: 'Along with' is a connector, not a joining conjunction, so the verb agrees with the main subject 'The car' (singular) — 'has'.

questions.question: "You together with your brother ___ able to face it." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: The main subject is 'You', which takes 'are' — the connector phrase 'together with your brother' does not change the verb.

questions.question: "The knowledge of four languages ___ required to join this service." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: In 'The + Noun + of + Noun' pattern, the verb agrees with the first noun — 'knowledge' is singular, so 'is' is correct.

questions.question: "Not only these children but also this boy ___ to gym daily." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: With 'Not only...but also', the verb agrees with the nearest subject — here 'this boy', which is singular, so 'goes'.

questions.question: "Neither Sam nor I ___ interested in attending the meeting." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: 'Neither...nor' follows the nearest-subject rule — the subject closest to the verb is 'I', so the verb is 'am'.

questions.question: "Bread and butter ___ not easy to earn these days." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: 'Bread and butter' is a pair noun expressing one combined concept (livelihood), so it takes a singular verb — 'is'.

questions.question: "The teacher and the peon ___ not come today." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: 'The teacher and the peon' (with two articles) names two different entities, so a plural verb — 'have' — is used. One article ('The clerk and student') would mean one person.

questions.question: "Patience as well as perseverance ___ necessary for success." Choose the correct verb.
questions.rationale: With connectors like 'as well as', the verb agrees with the main subject — 'Patience' (singular), so 'is' is correct.
